changes.investigation: first-party backend hostname discovery and exact next probe target
positiveEvidenceAppend: A live indexed first-party host https://api.enermia.org/ identifies itself as 'Enermia API'. This is a materially stronger backend lead than the generic APK distribution surfaces because Enermia is one of the entities merged into UAU/Uattzy and the current Uattzy Android package remains com.fortum.enermia.

Current Uattzy first-party FAQ explicitly states that the Uattzy app displays the tariff applied to each connector before charging and may also display activation/parking fees, confirming that a connector-level tariff payload exists somewhere in the current application/backend path.

Current Uattzy first-party site states that Uattzy is the public-charging brand of UAU created from E-Shore, GASGAS and EnerMia; this keeps api.enermia.org relevant to the ESH/GAS/UTZ technical lineage without proving that every current connector is served by that host.
negativeEvidenceAppend: No indexed path below api.enermia.org currently exposes connector IDs or tariff payloads through the web search surface.

Direct execution-container probing of api.enermia.org (root, /swagger, /swagger/index.html, /openapi.json and /robots.txt) is blocked by transient DNS resolution failure, so no endpoint schema or payload was inferred.
No tariff or ESH/GAS/UTZ mapping is promoted from the backend hostname alone.
